FORE'WORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 Decerrber 15 81, after the draft finalized by the Alloy Steels and Special Steels Sectional Commitee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council.
0.2 This standard was first published in 1574. On the basis of experience gained in the production and use of high speed steels, the following major modifications have been incorporated in this revision: a) Scope of the standard has been enlarged to include the requirements of high speed tool steels in the form of sheets and strips; b) The requirements for machining limits have been modified; allowances and decarburization

c) The requirements for minimum hardness in the hardened and tempered condition have been incorporated in Table 4 of this standard. These requirements are likely to be reviewed in future, after sufficient experience is available for production of high speed steel in the country; and d) Table 14 and Table 15 specifying tolerances on thickness and width for sheets and strips have been incorporated. 0.3 For the benefit of the users of this standard, particulars to be specified by the purchaser while ordering steels are given in Appendix A. 0.4 For the convenience of the users, information standards is given in Appendix C. 3 on comparable foreign

4.2 Sufficient reduction and discard shall be made from each ingot to ensure freedom from piping, segregation and other harmful defects. 4.3 The material shall be reasonably free any surface internal defects. However, completely removed after machining. from harmful surface and defect present should be

4.4 The material may be conditicned to remove injurious surface defects by chipping, machining, grinding or any other means at a suitable stage during reduction from the ingot to the finished size. 4.4.1 If the material is conditioned by grinding or chipping, the depth of conditioning shall not exceed half the machining allowance per side and width of conditioning shall be at least four times its greatest depth. 5. 8. MACRO-STRUCTURE
8.1 The macrostructure in the annealed condition shall be clean and exhibit a uniform and dense structure free from excess porosity, pipe, It is checks, cracks, non-metallic inclusions and other injurious defects. recommended for guidance only that 15 to 30 ,minutes etching time is necessary for revealing macrostructure in the annealed condition. 9. 14.1 Retest for `Product Analysis - If the results of the product analysis do not meet the composition requirements given in Table 1, unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer, two new samples shall be taken on different pieces from the same cast. If the two analysis satisfy the requirements, the lot represented shall be If, either of the tests fails, the material shall be taken as not accepted. complying with this standard.

14.2 Retest for Physical Tests - If the samples selected under 13.2 fail to meet the specified requirements, two samples shall be seiected The consignment shall further from the same consignment* of material. be considered to conform' to the requirements if both the additional tests are satisfactory. If either of the samples fail, the manufacturer shall have the right, if he so desires, to heat-treat the product again but not more than twice in any suitable manner and after two fresh samples If the two tests satisfy the requirements of this standard, the for testing. IS : 729111981 15. ADDITIONAL TESTS

15.1 Fracture in Heat-Treated Condition - If it is agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer that this test is required, the material after being heat-treated and fractured as described in 15.1.1 shall show a surface of uniform texture but shall not show any harmful defects, such as streaks, segregation, laminations, cracks, splits, pipes or seams. 15.1.1 The test specimens, wherever practicable, shall comprise the entire cross-sectional area of the material. For large sections, the fractured transverse cross-section shall include a segment containing the centre. The test pieces shall be suitably heat-treated according to the recommended heating schedule given in Appendix B and fractured. Hardened test pieces may be nicked with a thin cut-off wheel to assist in obtaining satisfactory fracture. The fresh fracture shall be examined visually and under 10 times magnification. 16. FINISH 16.1 The material may be supplied in any one of the following finishes: a) Hot rolled or forged, b) Cold drawn, c) Rough ground or rough turned, d) Precision ground or precision ground and polished, and e) Annealed. 17. PACKING 17.1 Barm - The material shall be packed in suitable bundles after they The bundles have been coated with a suitable rust preventive material. shall be covered with a suitable material like hessian and tied firmly with suitable size of wire at three or four places depending on the len th of .'entreAll bars of similar length shall be packed together.: E the bundles. less-ground bars, if required by the purchaser, shall be packed with polythene film and put in suitable wooden boxes. Hot rolled bars can also be packed in wooden boxes if mutually agreed betw&n purchaser and the supplier. 17.2 Sheet and Strip - Steel sheets in bundle and strips in coil form shall be suitably packed to prevent them flom rusting and damage during transit. 24

of the manufacturer,
